exact_local_scope.generic_statement: Let R be the root-reachable vertex subtype of an arbitrary quiver. If root-reachable a,b,c satisfy Reachable a c and Reachable b c, while neither Reachable a b nor Reachable b a, there is no select:R→Occurrence root that is both a right inverse to reachableEndpoint and preserves every base reachability comparison as occurrence reachability.
exact_local_scope.premises: No finiteness, countability, connectedness, acyclicity or thinness premise is needed. Root reachability is explicitly in R; the two common-upper comparisons and both incomparable comparisons are explicit hypotheses.
exact_local_scope.proof_reuse: The source applies the existing no_prefix_representation_of_incomparable_upper to address=trace∘select. Preservation follows from the assumed preservation and exact reachable_iff_prefix. Reflection is derived by decoding actual occurrence reachability, projecting an actual occurrence path with projection.mapPath, and rewriting endpoints with the right-inverse identities. It is not assumed from injectivity.
exact_local_scope.thin_diamond: The concrete instance reuses Diamond and DiamondLe with Hom a b=PLift(DiamondLe a b). Path induction using diamondLe_refl/trans and the converse actual one-edge path establish Reachable↔DiamondLe. Every vertex is root-reachable from bottom. The quiver includes identity loops and the bottom→top shortcut; it is not the four-edge Hasse DAG.
exact_local_scope.section_boundary: The current selectedOccurrence remains an actual endpoint right inverse. The conclusion rejects simultaneous preservation, not the existence of every set-theoretic endpoint section. Finite base vertices do not imply finitely many rooted histories.

actual_controls.positive: The positive module proves all four actual diamond comparisons/noncomparisons, rules out a preserving section, proves the actual selectedOccurrence endpoint right inverse, and proves that very selected section fails preservation. It also constructs the actual left/top and right/top length-two histories, proves they are distinct using their vertex lists, and confirms equal endpoints. Loop and shortcut examples verify the advertised quiver.
